conventions.positive-golden: tests/conformance/<edition>/<name>.cob + <name>.out; the directory selects --std. First line a comment `*> ISO §<clause> <rule> — <what is exercised>`. Unique PROGRAM-ID per program (a stale same-named assembly is served otherwise). Deterministic output only. Do NOT edit any manifest.json — return the entry; the director registers it.
conventions.negative-golden: tests/conformance/negative/<name>.cob + <name>.err (the expected diagnostic substring, e.g. COBOLNET1560). FIRST line of the .cob MUST be `*> reject-at: <year> [<year> ...]`. Do NOT edit the negative manifest — return the entry.
conventions.test-ref-forms: conformance:<edition>/<case> (positive, spec-derived) · conformance:negative/<case> · unit:<Class>.<Method> · conformance-test:<Class>.<Method>. nist:/characterization: and any *_MatchesLegacy method are NOT spec-derived and cannot close a row.
conventions.compiler: src/Cobol.Net.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/cobol.exe <file.cob> --std <85|2002|2014|2023> --run  (run in a scratch dir; never dotnet build/test — the tree is shared and a guard refuses builds while a fleet is live).
conventions.citation-check: python scripts/spec/cite.py --check <clause> "<quoted text>"  — every § you cite, no exceptions.

rows.subject: Variable-length data items
rows.adjudicator-notes: PERMISSIVE rule: §8.5.1.11.3 says the resources 'MAY be freed automatically when' the listed event occurs, and 'The actual time when the resources used by a variable-length data item are freed is implementor-defined' (Annex A item 220: required, need not be documented). The only binding content is that freeing is unobservable ('this has no effect on the results of the execution of the program') and persistence equals a fixed-length item's. COBOL.NET's variable-length items are managed .NET objects: a dynamic-length item IS a System.String field (CobolDynString), a dynamic-capacity table IS a CobolDynTable<T> (T[] + count); reclamation is by the CLR GC once unreachable, so every listed event is honoured at a GC-determined time, which the implementor-defined timing admits. cite.py --check 8.5.1.11.3 "The resources used by a variable-length data item may be freed automatically when" -> OK; --check 8.5.1.11.3 "The actual time when the resources used by a variable-length data item are freed is implementor-defined" -> OK; --check 8.5.1.11.1 "The term variable-length data item refers to either a dynamic-capacity table or a dynamic-length elementary item" -> OK. Editions: the facility is ISO 2014+ (Annex E item 17 of 2023 records only the SET SIZE enhancement as new, so the items pre-exist in 2014). Event 1 (object finalized): OBJECT working-storage variable-length items are per-instance managed fields; they become unreachable with the instance and are collected with it. Probe probe/vldi/p2.cob (CLASS-ID CDYN, OBJECT WS with OCCURS DYNAMIC + DYNAMIC LENGTH; two instances, FILL on O1, SHOW both, SET O1 TO NULL): output 'CAP=0000000006 D=[HELLO]' / 'CAP=0000000001 D=[]' -- per-instance storage, no sharing, released with the instance. No spec-derived test pins OO-instance variable-length data (none exists; the freeing itself is unobservable).
rows.rule-text: an object instance containing the data item is finalized;

Probe probe/vldi/p1.cob: INITIAL program VLDII grows its dynamic table to 5 and stores 'ABCD' in a DYNAMIC LENGTH item, GOBACK; second CALL prints 'INIT CAP=0000000001 LEN=0' both times -- storage released and the next activation starts fresh (persistence equals a fixed-length item's). No existing golden covers an INITIAL program with variable-length items.
rows.rule-text: the program containing the data item is an initial program and executes an EXIT PROGRAM or GOBACK;

rows.subject: Variable-length data items
rows.adjudicator-notes: PERMISSIVE rule: §8.5.1.11.3 says the resources 'MAY be freed automatically when' the listed event occurs, and 'The actual time when the resources used by a variable-length data item are freed is implementor-defined' (Annex A item 220: required, need not be documented). The only binding content is that freeing is unobservable ('this has no effect on the results of the execution of the program') and persistence equals a fixed-length item's. COBOL.NET's variable-length items are managed .NET objects: a dynamic-length item IS a System.String field (CobolDynString), a dynamic-capacity table IS a CobolDynTable<T> (T[] + count); reclamation is by the CLR GC once unreachable, so every listed event is honoured at a GC-determined time, which the implementor-defined timing admits. cite.py --check 8.5.1.11.3 "The resources used by a variable-length data item may be freed automatically when" -> OK; --check 8.5.1.11.3 "The actual time when the resources used by a variable-length data item are freed is implementor-defined" -> OK; --check 8.5.1.11.1 "The term variable-length data item refers to either a dynamic-capacity table or a dynamic-length elementary item" -> OK. Editions: the facility is ISO 2014+ (Annex E item 17 of 2023 records only the SET SIZE enhancement as new, so the items pre-exist in 2014). Event 6 (reduced in size): a dynamic-length shrink returns current[..n], a NEW string, so the old buffer is garbage immediately. A dynamic-capacity table shrink (SetCapacity n<_count) only lowers _count: the T[] backing array is not trimmed and the vacated slots keep their element values (and any string references) until the table itself is collected or the slots are re-seeded by GrowTo. That is RETENTION, which the permissive 'may be freed' plus implementor-defined timing admits; the binding half -- no observable effect -- holds because GrowTo re-seeds every slot in [old,new) through _seedAt before exposure. Probe probe/vldi/p1.cob: MOVE 'AB' TO E(4); SET CP TO 2; SET CP TO 4 -> 'E3=ZZ E4=ZZ' (the VALUE seed, not the stale 'AB'); dynamic-length MOVE 'HELLO', SET SIZE 2, SET SIZE 4 -> 'D=[HE  ]' (§14.9.39.4 GR39 spaces, truncated content not resurrected). Implicit reduction (MOVE of a shorter value) is the Store path, a new string. At --std 2014 SET SIZE is correctly COBOLNET0900 (Annex E item 17). Observation for the owner, not a defect: the untrimmed array means a table shrunk from a huge capacity keeps its peak memory for the table's lifetime -- a quality-of-implementation choice inside the latitude.
rows.rule-text: the variable-length data item is explicitly or implicitly reduced in size;

rows.subject: Variable-length data items
rows.adjudicator-notes: PERMISSIVE rule: §8.5.1.11.3 says the resources 'MAY be freed automatically when' the listed event occurs, and 'The actual time when the resources used by a variable-length data item are freed is implementor-defined' (Annex A item 220: required, need not be documented). The only binding content is that freeing is unobservable ('this has no effect on the results of the execution of the program') and persistence equals a fixed-length item's. COBOL.NET's variable-length items are managed .NET objects: a dynamic-length item IS a System.String field (CobolDynString), a dynamic-capacity table IS a CobolDynTable<T> (T[] + count); reclamation is by the CLR GC once unreachable, so every listed event is honoured at a GC-determined time, which the implementor-defined timing admits. cite.py --check 8.5.1.11.3 "The resources used by a variable-length data item may be freed automatically when" -> OK; --check 8.5.1.11.3 "The actual time when the resources used by a variable-length data item are freed is implementor-defined" -> OK; --check 8.5.1.11.1 "The term variable-length data item refers to either a dynamic-capacity table or a dynamic-length elementary item" -> OK. Editions: the facility is ISO 2014+ (Annex E item 17 of 2023 records only the SET SIZE enhancement as new, so the items pre-exist in 2014). Event 7 (overwritten with a new value) + the implementor-defined timing sentence: CobolDynString.Store returns the sender string (or its truncation) and the field is re-assigned, so the previous string is unreachable at once and collected by the GC at a GC-chosen time; a table overwrite (FromCurrentImage/element store) replaces element values in place. Probe probe/vldi/p1.cob: after 'HE  ' a MOVE 'Q' gives 'D=[Q] 1'. The second sentence ('The actual time ... is implementor-defined') is Annex A item 220 'required ... does not have to be documented', so no CONFORMANCE.md row is owed; COBOL.NET's answer is 'when the CLR garbage collector reclaims the unreachable object'.
rows.rule-text: the variable-length data item is overwritten with a new value. The actual time when the resources used by a variable-length data item are freed is implementor-defined.

rows.subject: Variable-length data items (actual time when the resources used are freed)
rows.adjudicator-notes: Voluntary row (A.1 220 need not be documented). cite.py --check 8.5.1.11.3 'The actual time when the resources used by a variable-length data item are freed is implementor-defined' -> OK §8.5.1.11.3 7). Read CobolDynTable: GrowTo only Array.Resize upward (doubling, capped at MaxOccurrences), re-seeds occurrences _count..target with _seedAt; SetCapacity shrink sets _count only (no array shrink); ValueInitializer.cs:139 'the field is a native string' for DYNAMIC LENGTH. Probe probe/p220/vl.cob --std 2023: D=XY L=002; C(5)=7, SET CAP TO 2, SET CAP TO 5 -> C5=0 CAP=5; --std 2002 -> COBOLNET0900 for both. Collection timing is nondeterministic, so no test can pin it. Resource exhaustion is item 61 / kb/Work/PB1410, not this item. Owning note: kb/Work/PB1535.
rows.rule-text: Variable-length data items (actual time when the resources used are freed). This item is required. This item does not have to be documented in the implementor's documentation. (8.5.1.11.3, Availability and persistence of variable-length data items)
